pr_title: Add signal to inform joint that body has exited tree
pr_body:
Currently there is no way to inform a `Joint` that a `PhysicsBody` attached to it has been removed. This PR connects the `tree_exiting` signal from a `PhysicsBody` attached to a configured `Joint` to provide this information and update the `Joint`.

Fixes #44510

Note: This also addresses:
1. The error message(s) raised in Bullet physics when trying to reconfigure a `Joint` that has had a `PhysicsBody` freed without first disconnecting it from the `Joint`; as described [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/43898#issue-528237028).
2. The warning message raised in Bullet physics when a scene was closed with a `PhysicsBody` attached to a `Joint` above it in the tree; as identified [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42285#issuecomment-742846838).

This PR includes raising the warning message in Bullet physics to an error; since this should now never occur.
pr_comments: Everything seems to work fine now! It should be good to go after the last little coding style fix.

issue_context.title: Crash in Godot Physics when removing a rigid body connected in a constraint
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
Master af2703c732893d089094f78cade8e08a84f3d2f1

**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10

**Issue description:**
This issue happens for both Godot Physics 2D and Godot Physics 3D. When removing a body which is still connected to another one with a joint and both are set to rigid bodies (not static or kinematic) the game crashes with no warning.

Crash callstack (it's similar for 2D and 3D):
```
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!Space2DSW::get_body_angular_velocity_sleep_threshold() Line 164	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!Body2DSW::sleep_test(float p_step) Line 618	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!Step2DSW::_check_suspend(Body2DSW * p_island, float p_delta) Line 105	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!Step2DSW::step(Space2DSW * p_space, float p_delta, int p_iterations) Line 287	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!PhysicsServer2DSW::step(float p_step) Line 1240	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!PhysicsServer2DWrapMT::step(float p_step) Line 76	C++
 godot.windows.tools.64.exe!Main::iteration() Line 2491	C++
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open MRP
2. Run JointTest2D.tscn or JointTest3D.tscn
3. Observe crash

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[JointTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5718810/JointTest.zip)

review_comments: `_disconnect_signals`also needs to be called in `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` for the joint (in 3D as well), to avoid cases where it's called later when the joint is not in the tree anymore, which causes errors with `get_node` (case where the joint is removed, then the bodies).

This is still triggered, because removing the rigid body from the physics world (`NOTIFICATION_EXIT_WORLD`) takes place before the joint has a chance to handle removed bodies.

It could be fixed by adding a new signal `_exit_world` to `CollisionObject3D` emitted before the body is removed from physics so the joints can connect to this one instead.

In 2D things are called in the right order already so there's no need for a change.

Do you have an MRP where this happens?

The `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_WORLD` is called during `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/41e9028868e49669de83c82ba20fd9dcef0d1b8b/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp#L153-L154
But `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` happens after `tree_exiting()` is emitted:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/41e9028868e49669de83c82ba20fd9dcef0d1b8b/scene/main/node.cpp#L267-L269
So, with this PR, the `PhysicsBodies` are detached from the `Joint` before they're removed from the space.

The only other scenario I can think of is: changing a `Viewport`'s world. A `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_WORLD` is propagated to the children of the `Viewport`, when a `Viewport`'s world is changed. However, since `Joint`s break when removing and adding them to a `SceneTree` (#41398), I'm not sure it's worth addressing as part of this PR, which is focused on addressing the crashing issue (#44510).
Yes, my bad. I think I might have made a mistake when testing on 3.2 and used `tree_exited` instead of `tree_exiting`. I've tested again and it works as you describe.
To be perfectly safe, this code could have a validity check like `ERR_FAIL_NULL(body)` (same for 3D) since it's calling an outside method to get the object.
